name: Ika / Arhuaco
confidence_why: 2 independent first-hand descriptions agree (0 state the same rule, 1 refine it); none contradicts.
catalog_citation: Landaburu, Jon. 1996. La langue ika ou arhuaco: phonologie. Amerindia 21. Paris: A.E.A. / CNRS-CELIA. (journal's re-typeset open web PDF, 16 pp; amerindia.cnrs.fr). Second source: Tracy, Hubert P. & Martha Tracy. 1973. Fonemas del ica (arhuaco). In Sistemas fonológicos de idiomas colombianos 2, 57-70. Lomalinda: ILV / Ministerio de Gobierno (scan + scan).
catalog_locator: Landaburu 1996 §1.1 'L'accent', pp. 1-2 (print pagination not shown in the re-typeset file); non-canonical examples §1.3 p. 3; renforcement passage §3.C, pp. 11-12. Tracy & Tracy 1973 §2 'El acento de grupo' pp. 58-59 and §4.3 p. 68.
catalog_quote: Tous les mots ika ont un accent. Celui-ci se manifeste par un élévation de la fréquence sonore sur une aire déterminée et/ou un renforcement de l'intensité de la prononciation sur cette même aire. [...] Nous disons alors que l'accent ika se trouve normalement sur l'avant-dernière syllabe du mot. Il s'agit bien sûr de la règle pour les mots polysyllabiques. Les monosyllabes sont normalement accentués et ce trait définit leur existence comme mot. Dans les mots de plus de trois syllabes, un accent secondaire peut apparaître. Il est alors normalement situé à deux syllabes de distance avant l'accent primaire. [...] Certains morphèmes grammaticaux monosyllabiques liés (clitiques, préfixes, suffixes) ne comptent pas comme syllabes métriques pour situer l'accent (ils ne comptent pas dans le calcul de la position canonique). Par ailleurs, pour indiquer des solidarités syntaxiques, il arrive que des mots se soudent en blocs dotés d'un seul accent primaire. [...] Nota bene: Dans les transcriptions phonétiques ou phonologiques de cet article, nous ne notons l'accent que quand il n'est pas en position canonique. Il est alors figuré par un accent graphique sur la voyelle: á, í, ó, etc.. Nous ne notons pas l'accent secondaire.
world_status: statement found in an open source

new_statements.translation: All Ika words have an accent. It is realised as a rise in pitch over a given span and/or a reinforcement of intensity over that same span. [...] We therefore say that the Ika accent normally falls on the penultimate syllable of the word. This is of course the rule for polysyllabic words. Monosyllables are normally accented, and this feature defines their existence as words. In words of more than three syllables a secondary accent may appear. It is then normally located two syllables before the primary accent.
new_statements.citation: Landaburu, Jon. 1996. La langue ika ou arhuaco: phonologie. Amerindia 21. Paris: A.E.A. (CNRS-CELIA).
new_statements.locator: §1.1 'L'accent', pp. 1-2 of the journal's web PDF (Amerindia 21; original print pagination not shown in this re-typeset file)
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: The quotation was checked again. Opened (16-page re-typeset Amerindia 21 PDF with text; extracted text pp. 1-2). Section '1.1. L'accent' reads exactly as quoted: 'Tous les mots ika ont un accent. Celui-ci se manifeste par un élévation de la fréquence sonore sur une aire déterminée et/ou un renforcement de l'intensité de la prononciation sur cette même aire.'.. 'Nous disons alors que l'accent ika se trouve normalement sur l'avant-dernière syllabe du mot. Il s'agit bien sûr de la règle pour les mots polysyllabiques. Les monosyllabes sont normalement accentués et ce trait définit leur existence comme mot. Dans les mots de plus de trois syllabes, un accent secondaire peut apparaître. Il est alo…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Primary word stress (pitch rise and/or intensity) falls on the penultimate syllable of the word; monosyllables are stressed. Certain bound monosyllabic grammatical morphemes (clitics, prefixes, suffixes) are invisible to the syllable count that locates stress, so surface position can deviate from strict penult; the author writes an accent mark only when stress is not in canonical (penultimate) position.
new_statements.secondary_stress: In words of more than three syllables a secondary stress may appear, normally two syllables before the primary stress (e.g. "kiNku'mʉya'ni 'he arrives', "uNkʉ'sia 'protective bracelet'); the author does not transcribe it.
new_statements.exceptions: (i) Certain bound monosyllabic grammatical morphemes (clitics, prefixes, suffixes) do not count as metrical syllables for locating the accent; (ii) to mark syntactic cohesion, words may fuse into blocks bearing a single primary accent (ko'kuru 'kawa 'it is round' vs. kokuruk'awa 'the round one'); (iii) accent is transcribed with an acute (á, í, ó) only when it is NOT in canonical penultimate position, implying some non-canonical cases exist. Landaburu 2000: 733-734 (Spanish, also saved and scanned) restates the same rule verbatim in substance: 'el acento se coloca normalmente sobre la penúltima sílaba de la palabra y sobre la única sílaba en caso de monosílabos'.
new_statements.domain_note: Domain is the word ('mot'); accent defines wordhood for monosyllables. Phrase-level: syntactically cohesive word groups can merge into a single accentual block with one primary accent. Accent is described as culminative (every word has one), realised by F0 rise and/or intensity; no claim of lexical contrast beyond the non-canonical cases.
new_statements.identity_note: Both Landaburu sources describe 'ika' = Arhuaco (arhu1242, ISO arh), Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta, Colombia; Landaburu 2000 notes little internal dialect variation. No dialect restriction stated; data from Landaburu's own fieldwork (CCELA/Universidad de los Andes).

new_statements.quote: Rasgo suprasegmental / Acento (signo ortográfico correspondiente al español) /´/ (observaciones) se usa cuando el acento no sea sobre la penúltima sílaba de la palabra [p. 147]. — (1) en la primera sílaba inacentuada de una palabra de tres sílabas /abitti/ [a'bittʰi ~ aa'bittʰi] 'nuevo'. (2) en la sílaba final acentuada de una palabra /kuk'ke/ [kʰuk'kʰe ~ kʰuk'kʰee] 'apurado' [pp. 144-145]
new_statements.translation: Suprasegmental feature / Accent (orthographic sign corresponding to Spanish) /´/ (remarks) is used when the accent is not on the penultimate syllable of the word. — (1) in the first, unstressed syllable of a three-syllable word /abitti/ 'new'. (2) in the stressed final syllable of a word /kuk'ke/ 'in a hurry'.

new_statements.second_reader_evidence: 15 = printed p. 147, rendered and read on the page scan: item '70 Rasgo suprasegmental / Acento (signo ortografico correspondiente al espanol) /'/ (observaciones) se usa cuando el acento no sea sobre la penultima silaba de la palabra' is verbatim. pp. 12-13 = printed pp. 144-145, section '2. El alargamiento fonetico de las vocales': '(1) en la primera silaba inacentuada de una palabra de tres silabas /abitti/ [a'bɨttʰi ~ aa'bɨttʰi] 'nuevo'. (2) en la silaba final acentuada de una palabra /kuk'ke/ [kʰuk'kʰe ~ kʰuk'kʰee] 'apurado'' verbatim; the only differences are transcription details (the page has barred ɨ in [a'bɨttʰi], which the compiler wrote as i, and kaƀa with barred b in /'kokoro ka…
new_statements.relation_note: Same placement as the catalog record (penult, Landaburu 1996 statement). Refines it by making explicit that non-penult stress occurs and is lexically marked in the orthography, and by listing final- and initial-stressed words; the catalog penultimate stress encodes only the penult default and no exceptions.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Stress falls on the penultimate syllable by default; the written accent is reserved for words whose stress is elsewhere, i.e. non-penult stress exists and is lexically marked. The article is a set of corrections to the 1973 phoneme paper and contains no separate stress section; the statement is the orthographic rule for the accent mark.
new_statements.exceptions: Non-penult stress is treated as the marked case and several cited forms show it: final stress in /kuk'ke/ 'apurado' (p. 145), /ri'bin/ 'aprender' and /pui a?'karin/ (p. 147); initial (antepenult) stress in /'punkiri/ 'tipo de yerba' (p. 144), /'pipiri/ 'un tipo de pájaro', /'kokoro kaba/ 'redondo', /'čikkiru 'kaba/ 'verde' (Dialecto A) (p. 147).
new_statements.identity_note: Tracy & Tracy 1976 labels two forms 'Dialecto A' and 'Dialecto B' (p. 147, p. 146) without tying stress placement to dialect. Tracy & Levinsohn 1977 (footnote 3) rests on data collected since February 1968 with helpers Briceño Torres Villafaña and Abran and Horacio Izquierdo Solis; footnote 1 notes the people's own word ['ikʰɨ] and the names Arhuaco, Ijca, Ijka, Iké.

sources.note: §1.1.1.1 El acento (pp. 2-3, printed pp. 733-734): 'Todas las palabras del ika llevan un acento.. el acento se coloca normalmente sobre la penúltima sílaba de la palabra y sobre la única sílaba en caso de monosílabos. Ciertos morfemas gramaticales ligados monosilábicos (enclíticos, prefijos, sufijos) no tienen peso propio en el conteo silábico que ubica el acento.' Same analysis as 1996, in Spanish.
